Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:
Yes, this is an old one.
I'm trying to understand what exactly happens between the two combats.

Here's the original discussion:

> [url=http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/bcc9e6babcd7b1d8 wrote:
> Rulemonger[/url]"]> How about playing a Psyche when combat is ending due to agg damage?
>
> No. Psyche! requires both minions to be ready.
> Combat is ending "due to agg damage" means that one of the combatants
> is no longer ready (which is how agg damage ends combat).
> > or a UP and a Psyche at superior?
>
> Yes. The UP'ed vampire will not fall into torpor from UP's effect
> until after the Psyche! combat. But, and I'd overlooked this before,
> the Psyche! combat ends as soon as it begins, since the formerly-UPed
> vampire is no longer being propped up by the UP. Since he's no longer
> ready, combat ends (unless he plays another UP for this new combat,
> of course).
Here is the situation:
A (acting) and B (blocking) are in combat. In that combat, B should be wounded due to a 1agg strike (let's not consider Rowan Ring / Stake, so far). B plays Undead Persistence. B is still wounded, and should go to torpor (per the rules), but UP prevents that.
Then, combat ends. A plays sup' Psyche!

We are now before the combat Psyche! would generate. In this step, B could play Wakes, Obedience ([LSJ 19991025] (http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/7fa25a6d1ae41b2b)), or the Ohoyo Hopoksia could be used.
In this step, B is wounded (since he was inflicted that 1agg strike).
However, the source discussion explicitely reads B won't go to torpor until after the Psyche! combat.

What I don't get is why B isn't sent to torpor before the Psyche! combat. He is wounded, with no effect that would prevent him from being sent to torpor.

Suppose the Ohoyo enters combat instead of B, in that Psyche! combat.
When exactly does B go to torpor?

Thanks !
Pascal

~~

Undead Persistence
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Fortitude
[for] Only usable when this vampire should go into torpor. This vampire gets an optional press and will not go to torpor until combat ends (although he or she is still considered wounded and can be burned as normal). If three rounds of combat pass with no cards played, combat ends. This vampire is sent into torpor after combat.
[FOR] Prevent 2 damage.

Psyche!
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Celerity
[cel] Press.
[CEL] Only usable at the end of combat when both combatants are still ready. Begin another combat with the opposing minion.

Obedience
Cardtype: Reaction
Discipline: Dominate
Only usable when this reacting vampire is about to enter combat with an acting younger vampire.
[dom] Untap the acting vampire, do not tap this reacting vampire, and end the current action (and combat). The acting vampire cannot attempt the same action this turn.
[DOM] As above, but do not untap the acting vampire.

Ohoyo Hopoksia (Bastet)
Cardtype: Ally
Clan: Ahrimane
Cost: 3 pool
Unique werewolf with 3 life. 3 strength, 0 bleed.
When a minion you control is about to enter combat with an acting minion, you may tap Ohoyo to cancel that combat; Ohoyo enters combat with the acting minion instead. She gets an optional maneuver each combat. If she has less than 3 life during your untap phase, she gains 1 life from the blood bank.

Messages.Author: Rulemonger
Messages.Body:
You misread the cited source.

It says that B is wounded and thus combat ends, since B is not ready.

Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:
Let's do that explicitely ..

A (has an Ivory Bow, is acting, has CEL) and B (blocking, has for) are in combat.
A's strike is to use the Ivory Bow. B doesn't prevent, but plays Undead Persistence (inf).
This combat doesn't end right now - let's skip to its end.

At the end of this combat,
a/ Can A play Psyche! ? I assumed, from the quote above, that A can.
b/ I read the quote as : "If A plays Psyche!, B will immediately go to torpor in the new combat (causing the Psyche! combat to end as it begins), since B is wounded - unless he plays a new UP in that new combat.". Did I get something wrong there?
c/ A plays Psyche! Can B (wounded) play Obedience?

My understanding would be that B goes to torpor as soon as the first combat ends (but perhaps after Psyche! gets to be played - that's a little bit obscure). B couldn't play Obedience, the Ohoyo couldn't be used. Depending on when B goes to torpor, A might or might not be able to play Psyche!.

Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:
Ah! I knew it ringed a bell!

However, there's this part between the two combats that I still don't get.
When B would play Obedience, we are clearly not in a combat (otherwise, Obedience couldn't be played). Thus, UP from the first combat is not keeping B ready any more.

Is there an effect that maintains wounded B in the ready region, there, between the first combat (that has ended) and the Psyche! combat (that hasn't yet begun) ?

Messages.Author: jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
Scott,
I think Floppy is trying to make you commit to one of the following 3 statements:

A) Undead Persistence is playable during the same timing window that Psyche is played, in order to continue a previous Undead Persistence effect.

B) Psyche can be played, but combat immediately ends when the Undead Persistent vampire immediately falls into torpor.

or

C) It is illegal to play Psyche in this situation, because the requirements for "enter combat" are not met (one of the vampires is not ready when combat ends).

Personally, I think C is the best answer.
But I am not the one who makes the rulings :)

Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:
I'm not reducing it to a choice of one out of three (plus, my opinion is that none of A and B are acceptable - A because the new combat hasn't started when Psyche! is played, due to that ruling about Obedience; B because it's not worded the way I'd word it, I'd have "Psyche! can be played, but combat ends with persistent vampire falling into torpor" - and the only one left is difficult to consider as an intuitive option, since it would involve a new ruling).

There is already cases where a combat is queued and will happen between a ready vampire and a vampire in torpor (Psychomachia or Siren's Lure are the first examples to come to me).
My opinion would be that it would be the most intuitive to have the vampire who played UP go to torpor as the combat ends - as it reads on the card.

But a ruling could make it otherwise (hence the question about what makes the wounded vampire remain ready between the two combats). Or, if my intuition were correct (this would deserve unusual celebrations), then the playability of Psyche! remains to be discussed.

Messages.Author: Rulemonger
Messages.Body:
> floppyzedolfin wrote:
> Ah! I knew it ringed a bell!
>
> However, there's this part between the two combats that I still don't get.
> When B would play Obedience, we are clearly not in a combat (otherwise, Obedience couldn't be played). Thus, UP from the first combat is not keeping B ready any more.
When B would play Obedience that means there is a combat "about to begin". And there is: the Psyche! combat (begun by the Psyche! effect; Psyche! being a card that resolves when played).

> Is there an effect that maintains wounded B in the ready region, there, between the first combat (that has ended) and the Psyche! combat (that hasn't yet begun) ?
Moot. Psyche! is played at the end of one combat and begins another.

Messages.Author: drnlmza
Messages.Body:
So, since I personally still feel a bit confused here, I'm going to toss a few more examples in to see if I'm understanding things correctly:

Case 1:

Ibn Khaldun (for TEM) is blocked by Hektor (for CEL, agg hand damage). Each declares a hand strike.
Ibn Khaldun plays inf Undead Pesistance, and declines to press. Hektor plays Superior Psyche, and a new combat starts.

I assume Ibn cannot play Outside the Hourglass or any other pre-range cards before playing Undead Persistance, since, at the start of combat, he's going to torpor, and must play an Undead Persistance (or Undying Tenacity) to continue combat first.

Case 2:

Ibn Khaldun (for TEM) is blocked by Hektor (for CEL, agg hand damage) and plays Domain of Evernght at inf. Nothing before range and each strike hands for 1. Ibn Khaldun prevents the damage with Resilence. Hektor plays Undead Persistance and declines to press.

Hektor plays Superior Psyche, and a new combat starts.

Since Ibn Khaldun is the acting minion, presumably he can play pre-range cards before Hektor has to play an effect to avoid going to torpor?

If that is correct, and Ibn plays Outside the Hourglass, and Hektor doesn't play another Undead Persistance, does the damage from OtH resolve? I think it would, but I'm not particularly sure.

Case 3:

Ibn Khaldun (for TEM) is blocked by Hektor (for CEL, agg hand damage) - and plays Domain of Evernght at inf. Nothing before range and each strike hands for 1. Ibn Khaldun prevents the damage with Resilence. Hektor plays Undead Persistance and declines to press.

Can Synesios play Hidden Lurker?

It seems legal in the circumstances. I assume this would work exactly like a combat started by Psyche - unless Hektor plays a card to prop himself up, combat immediately ends with Hektor going to torpor.

Case 4:

Ibn Khaldun (for TEM) is blocked by Hektor (for CEL, agg hand damage)  and plays superior Pocket out of Time and Domain of Evernight inf. Nothing before range and each strike hands for 1. Ibn Khaldun prevents the damage with Resilence. Hektor plays Undead Persistance and declines to press.

Can Ibn burn a blood to restart combat from Pocket Out of Time?

Presumably not, since unlike Hidden Lurker, Pocket out of Time specifies ready, and as Hektor is wounded, he isn't ready.

Case 5:

Ibn Khaldun (for TEM) is blocked by Hektor (for CEL, agg hand damage) and plays superior Pocket out of Time. Nothing before range and each strike hands for 1. Ibn Khaldun plays inf Undead Pesistance, and declines to press.

Can Ibn burn a blood to start a new combat with Pocket out of Time?

Presumably not, as Ibn doesn't qualify as ready.

Messages.Author: Rulemonger
Messages.Body:
When the new Psyche! combat starts, it is ending (with B not ready), so "as-ending" effects may be played (like Undead Persistence).

Other effects cannot be played as ending.
